newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman boosts North Sea position.
newsitem.headline: Talisman boosts North Sea position.

text.p: Canada's Talisman Energy Inc said on Thursday it agreed to purchase operated interests in North Sea oil fields from U.K. units of Texaco Inc.

Talisman said the new assets, in the UKCS Quadrant 13 to the west of Talisman's Ross Field and Quadrant 20 adjacent to its Buchan field, would combine with existing fields to establish the Moray Firth region as a core operating area.
As part of the deal, Talisman will transfer its 10-percent stake in Block 15/28a to Texaco and drill a licence obligation well on Block 13/26a, it said.

Talisman last year acquired a 52 percent stake in the undeveloped Ross field, estimated to harbor reserves of 60 million-100 million barrels of crude oil. The company received UK government approval for its development in June.
First production was expected in September 1998 with Talisman's share of peak output pegged at over 20,000 barrels a day, it said.
Talisman said the exploration potential of the Moray Firth basin was enhanced by the recent discovery of oil on adjacent Block 13/24b, located 11 kms north of the Ross field.
That discovery, by partners BG Plc, Amerada Hess Corp and Rigel Energy Corp, could hold recoverable reserves of 270 million-330 million barrels, Rigel said in late May.

"The Moray Firth region is relatively unexplored and is generating growing excitement," Talisman Chief Executive Jim Buckee said in a statement. "We see potential in this area and are acting on it. These are suitable and attractive targets for a company of Talisman's size and capabilities."
Talisman said it would carry out an extensive program to explore and appraise a number of identified opportunities in the region.
The license assignments as part of the transaction with Texaco were subject to UK Department of Trade and Industry approval, Talisman said.

Talisman's North Sea production in the first quarter averaged 52,000 barrels of oil and 118 million cubic feet of natural gas a day. Company-wide outout is currently 200,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day, up 20 percent from last year, Talisman said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
